cards.context: The lateral rectus lies on the temporal side of the globe. It moves the eye away from the nose and is supplied by the abducens nerve (CN VI).

reference.title: Cranial Nerves III, IV, and VI: Oculomotor Function

cards.front: Compared with a sixth-nerve nucleus lesion, an isolated peripheral sixth-nerve lesion preserves contralateral eye [___].
cards.context: A lesion of the peripheral sixth nerve weakens the ipsilateral lateral rectus. The opposite eye can still adduct because the contralateral medial rectus pathway is not part of that peripheral nerve.
